TAK Server is the hub that TAK clients (ATAK, WinTAK, iTAK, TAK Tracker) connect to in order to share situational awareness. For an integrator it has two interfaces, and you'll usually use both.

1. Real-time CoT streaming

The live heartbeat of TAK is Cursor-on-Target (CoT) — compact event messages ("what is where, when, by whom": positions, markers, chat, sensor data). Clients open a persistent TCP/TLS streaming connection to TAK Server and exchange CoT continuously.

  • Transport is TLS with mutual authentication (the client presents an X.509 certificate). The streaming port is configured per deployment (commonly 8089).
  • What you receive is filtered by your groups (see Keycloak: identity & groups) — you only see traffic for groups you read from.
  • As an integrator you can act as a "client": connect, subscribe, and send/receive CoT just like an ATAK device would.

CoT itself is covered from the client side in the ATAK plugin guide (CoT in depth); the wire format is the same on the server link.

2. The Marti REST API

Everything that isn't the live CoT stream — managing shared data, files, missions, groups, feeds, federation — is done through TAK Server's REST API, historically called Marti. Every endpoint lives under **/Marti/api/…** and is documented in the spec.

The main capability areas (tags in the spec):

Area What it's for
Missions / Data Sync (/Marti/api/missions/…) Shared, persistent "missions": collections of map content, files, layers, logs — the primary way to share structured data with a team. Supports nesting, roles, invites, passwords, keywords.
Enterprise Sync (/Marti/api/sync/…, /files/…) Content-addressed file store — data packages, attachments, imagery — referenced by hash.
Subscriptions (/Marti/api/subscriptions/…) Register/inspect CoT subscriptions and per-client filters.
Groups (/Marti/api/groups/…) The access-control partitions that decide who sees/sends what.
Inputs / Data Feeds / Outgoing connections Configure how data enters and leaves the server (ports, feeds, predicates).
Federation (/Marti/api/federation…) Connect TAK Servers together so missions/data flow between them.
Video, Device Profiles, Metadata, Retention, ExCheck Video feeds, client provisioning profiles, metadata, data-lifecycle, checklists.
OAuth API (OIDC) Token-based auth + OpenID Connect configuration — how TAK Server federates identity to an IdP like Keycloak.

Authentication model

TAK Server is certificate-first:

  • mTLS client certificates are the primary credential, for both the CoT stream and the Marti API. Your certificate identifies you and ties you to your groups.
  • TAK Server can also issue client certs itself (POST /Marti/api/tls/signClient), but on a Deploy App deployment you get your certificate from Deploy App instead (see Enrolling & getting a client certificate).
  • OAuth/OIDC is supported for token-based access and browser logins; TAK Server reads an OpenID provider's configuration (Keycloak, in a Deploy App deployment).

Ports & protocols

TAK Server listens on several ports; the ones an integrator touches:

Port Purpose
8089 CoT TCP+TLS streaming — the encrypted real-time client connection (a tls input).
8443 HTTPS with X.509 client-certificate auth — the Marti API, the admin UI, and WebTAK.
8446 HTTPS with OAuth / username-password — including the OAuth2 token endpoint /oauth/token.
9000 / 9001 Federation (protocol v1 / v2) — server-to-server only, not for clients.

The default ports to open for a basic deployment are 8089 and 8443. (On a Deploy App deployment the Marti API is reached at https://<server>:8443/Marti/….)

Streaming inputs can use different protocols: **tls** (encrypted — what real clients use, on 8089), stcp (unencrypted streaming, testing only), and tcp/udp/mcast (unencrypted). Use tls for anything real — the unencrypted protocols are a security risk.

Federation (server-to-server)

Separate TAK Servers — possibly run by different organizations — can federate so subsets of their users share data, without either side exposing its internal structure or allowing the other's clients to connect directly. Each side controls what it shares via federated group mapping. It's an admin/server topic rather than a client integration, but it's why data may reach you from a server other than your own.

How the pieces relate

TAK clients ──CoT over TLS──▶  TAK Server  ◀──REST (/Marti/api)── your integration
                                  │
                          groups decide visibility
                                  │
                              Keycloak (OIDC, groups)
                                  ▲
                     Deploy App / RASENMAEHER issues the mTLS cert
